title: Beneficiaries of government contracts
summary: A person who benefits from a government contract does not necessarily acquire a private contractual right to enforce it.
notes: Sisney v. State and Sisney v. Reisch examine different agreements and evidence of intended rights. The analysis asks what the contracting parties undertook and whether the intended benefit supports enforceability by this claimant; general public benefit and an individual enforcement right are distinct.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.
